fumagillin is synthesized by a pathway involving the following reactions: (a) cyclization of farnesyl pyrophosphate, followed by (b) reduction of the double bond in the resulting farnesyl diphosphate and (c) oxidation to the fumagillin nucleus.
the biosynthesis of fumagilin involves the terpene pathway for the production of the carbon skeleton of its nucleus and a pathway involving ‘acetate’ for the production of its side-chain.

the side chain of the antibiotic is derived from acetate without the intervention of a symethylated symmetrical intermediate, and that the nucleus is formed by the terpense route, with the C15 carbon atom of fumagillol (II; R = H) derived from mevalonate and the remaining carbon atoms from acetyl CoA.
